intro: Numbers and time are everywhere. You need them to pay at a taquería in Little Village, to trade phone numbers with a new friend, to tell your age, and to know when the bus leaves. In this unit you will count from cero to mil, read prices, do quick math out loud, tell time, and name the days, months and dates of the year in Spanish.

Spanish numbers work like building blocks. Once you know a few small words, you can join them to say big numbers: treinta y cinco (35), ciento veinte (120), quinientos (500). Clocks and calendars have their own patterns too: Es la una, Son las tres y media, el dieciséis de septiembre. Each pattern is short, and this unit walks through each one with real examples.

By the end, you will be able to plan an event in Spanish: say what day, what date and what time it happens, and how much it costs. You will also know why Spanish writes dates day-first, why days and months are lowercase, and what holidays like Día de los Muertos and Mexico's Independence Day celebrate.
bigQuestion: How do numbers, clocks and calendars in Spanish help us plan, buy and celebrate together?

timeline.t: A manuscript copied in northern Spain includes some of the earliest Hindu-Arabic numerals written in Europe
Antonio de Nebrija publishes the first grammar of the Castilian Spanish language
Spain is among the first countries to adopt the new Gregorian calendar
Miguel de Cervantes publishes the first part of Don Quijote
The Real Academia Española (RAE) is founded in Madrid
The fight for Mexican independence begins; September 16 becomes Independence Day
Mexico achieves its independence from Spain
Mexican forces win the Battle of Puebla on May 5, remembered as Cinco de Mayo
Spain replaces the peseta with euro coins and bills

words.d: fifteen — a single word to memorize
twenty-two — one word with an accent
one hundred exactly; ciento when more follows
to be … years old: Tengo doce años
the hour; clock time: ¿Qué hora es?
half past: las dos y media
a quarter to: las seis menos cuarto is 5:45
the date: el doce de octubre, written 12/10
the birthday — singular even though it ends in -s

test.why: Twenty-three is one word with an accent: veintitrés.
Exactly one hundred is cien, with no un.
Thousands are counted with mil and no plural: dos mil.

test.q: How do you ask how much the shoes (los zapatos) cost?
test.why: For more than one thing, use cuestan.

test.q: Which sentence correctly says My sister is sixteen?
test.why: Age uses tener + number + años; dieciséis is sixteen.

test.q: What does "Doce menos cinco son siete" mean?
It is 1:15. What do you say?
test.why: One o'clock is singular, and quarter past is y cuarto.

test.q: What time is "Son las siete menos veinte"?

test.why: Ten at night is las diez de la noche.
Days are lowercase and need no extra word: Hoy es martes.

test.q: A note from Mexico says the meeting is on 9/11. When is it?
test.why: Dates in Mexico are written day-first: 9/11 is the ninth of November.

test.q: How do you say My birthday is January 1?
choices: Mi cumpleaños es el Primero de Enero.
Mi cumpleaños es el primero de enero.
Mis cumpleaños es el primero de enero.
test.why: Use el primero for the first, de, and a lowercase month; cumpleaños takes singular mi.

test.q: What happens on September 16 in Mexico?
test.why: September 16 is Mexico's Independence Day, remembering 1810.

test.q: Which item is part of an ofrenda for Día de los Muertos?
choices: A carved pumpkin with a scary face
test.why: An ofrenda holds photos of loved ones, candles, food and marigold flowers.

write.prompt: Write an invitation in Spanish (5–7 sentences) to a party or event. Say what it is, the day and date (el … de …), the time with de la mañana, tarde or noche, how much any tickets or food cost, and how old the birthday person is if it is a birthday.
tips: Write days and months in lowercase.
Put the day before the month: el catorce de febrero.
Use es la una for one o'clock and son las for other hours.
Use tener for age and check cien versus ciento.
Read your numbers aloud to check every accent.
